findings.title: New abstract getShortcut breaks existing grant provider factories
findings.body: The new abstract `getShortcut()` method on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` has no default implementation. Existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations compiled against an older Keycloak version do not implement it; `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls `gtf.getShortcut()` for every registered grant, so such a provider will fail at server startup with `AbstractMethodError` (and source builds will no longer compile). Add a default implementation or avoid calling the method for factories that do not support it, and provide a migration path.

findings.title: Grant shortcut length is not validated against the fixed 6-character format
findings.body: `encodeTokenId` concatenates `grantShort` without checking that it is exactly two characters, while `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` requires the encoded context to be exactly six characters (`sessionType` 2 + `tokenType` 2 + `grantType` 2). The new `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` Javadoc explicitly says a shortcut is usually like 3 letters; a provider following that contract produces an ID such as `onrtabc:<uuid>`, which later fails parsing with `Expected length of 6` (or misreads the grant segment). Validate shortcut length when building the maps (or make the encoder/parser length-aware) and align the Javadoc. There is no test for a non-2-character shortcut.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
findings.body: `isAccessTokenId` does not validate the expected grant type. For a valid prefix such as `onrtac`, the grant shortcut is at indexes 4-6 (`ac`), but the matcher reads `substring(3, 5)` (`ta`); it also returns `false` when the compared segment equals `expectedGrantShortcut`, which is inverted. Consequently any token ID of the form `<six chars>:<uuid>` passes regardless of the encoded grant type, so the updated event assertions cannot detect wrong or missing grant encoding. It can also throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` for a colon-containing ID with a short prefix. Use `substring(4, 6)` and reject only when the segment is not equal.

findings.title: Null check on rawTokenId is missing
findings.body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...)` twice instead of checking `rawTokenId`. A null raw token ID is therefore accepted; `encodeTokenId` later silently appends the literal `null` (for example `onrtac:null`) instead of failing, and the error message for a null grant type incorrectly says rawTokenId is null.

findings.title: Public Context copy constructor was removed
findings.body: This diff removes the public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` copy constructor. External `OAuth2GrantType` implementations or tests that clone a request context will no longer compile, and there is no replacement constructor that also copies the newly added `grantType` field. Keep and deprecate the constructor, or add an equivalent replacement.
